name: FAFSA / Federal Pell Grant
what: Free Application for Federal Student Aid unlocks Pell Grants (need-based, no repayment), federal work-study, and subsidized/unsubsidized loans.

name: Federal Work-Study
what: Subsidized part-time campus/community jobs for students with financial need; wages don't count against next year's aid as heavily as other income.

name: Housing Choice Voucher Program (Section 8)
what: Federal rent subsidy so tenant pays ~30% of income; landlord receives the rest directly.

name: SNAP (federally funded, state-administered)
what: Monthly EBT card funds for groceries at participating retailers.

name: WIC (Women, Infants & Children)
what: Food vouchers, formula, and nutrition counseling for pregnant/postpartum people and children under 5.

name: Lifeline
what: Discount on monthly phone or internet bill — up to $9.25/mo, or $34.25/mo on Tribal lands.

name: Earned Income Tax Credit (EITC) & Child Tax Credit
what: Refundable tax credits that can return several thousand dollars to low/moderate-income workers and families at filing time.

name: Medicaid (federal/state)
what: Free or low-cost health coverage; NM expanded eligibility to adults up to 138% FPL.

name: NM Human Services / Health Care Authority — ISD Programs
what: Umbrella state agency administering SNAP, TANF (cash assistance), Medicaid, General Assistance, and LIHEAP (energy).
contact: 877-993-3637 (ISD) · Albuquerque NE office: 4330 Cutler Ave NE, 505-222-9600 · SW office: 3280 Bridge Blvd SW, 505-841-2

name: LIHEAP (Low Income Home Energy Assistance)
what: Helps pay heating/cooling bills; max benefit around $600, applications open Nov–March.

name: NM Legislative Lottery Scholarship
what: Covers a large share of tuition at NM public colleges for eligible in-state students.

name: NM Opportunity Scholarship
what: 'Last-dollar' scholarship that can cover remaining tuition/fees after other aid, including for part-time and adult students.

name: Grow Your Own Teachers Scholarship
what: Funds aspiring teachers, especially in high-need NM districts.

name: Fire Fighters and Peace Officers Survivors Scholarship
what: Tuition support for dependents/survivors of fallen first responders.

name: NM Homeowner Assistance Fund
what: Helps existing homeowners catch up on mortgage, property tax, or utility payments to avoid foreclosure.

name: New Mexico Home Fund
what: Covers past-due/current/future rent, utility bills, relocation costs, and temporary lodging after eviction.
contact: See loborespect.unm.edu housing page for current link

name: 211 New Mexico / United Way of Central NM
what: Free 24/7 phone & web referral hub connecting to virtually every category below (food, rent, utilities, healthcare, legal, childcare).

name: City of Albuquerque 311
what: General city information line that can route callers to any Family & Community Services program.

name: Dept. of Family & Community Services
what: Umbrella department running the city's Health & Social Service Centers, housing programs, recreation, and education services.

name: Youth & Family Resource Roundup
what: Directory of before/after-school programs (ages 5-15), Early Head Start/Preschool (0-5), Family Advocacy Center (DV/abuse survivors), and Violence Intervention Program.

name: Albuquerque Housing Authority
what: Public housing units (~950) and Section 8 voucher administration for low-income, elderly, and disabled residents. Tenant pays ~30% of income.

name: Office of Civil Rights
what: Handles discrimination complaints in housing, public accommodation, and employment.

name: Albuquerque Community Safety (ACS)
what: Alternative first-responder department for behavioral health, homelessness, and non-violent crisis calls (non-police).

name: UNM Short-Term Emergency Loan
what: Emergency loans up to $800 for enrolled students; partial forgiveness possible in some cases.

name: Center for Financial Capability (CFC)
what: One-on-one budgeting, scholarship search help, credit-building support, free tax prep (AARP Tax-Aide), and general basic-needs referrals.

name: Lobo Food Pantry
what: Free groceries for any enrolled student with valid Lobo ID, located SUB 1093. Also a monthly outdoor giveaway in the South Parking Lot.

name: El Centro de la Raza
what: Academic advising, cultural programming, and scholarship/funding navigation for UNM's largest ethnic student population.

name: Transformar Fellowship Program
what: 1-on-1 academic guidance/advocacy, a $600 completion scholarship, and an optional summer study-abroad trip to Mexico.

name: American Indian Student Services (AISS)
what: Cultural/academic programming, FAFSA help open to ALL students (not just Native students), scholarship connections, advocacy.

name: African American Student Services (Afro)
what: Academic advising, tutorial assistance, financial aid issue resolution, internship/mentorship connections, computer lab, meeting space, and FREE PRINTING for Black staff/students/community.

name: Women's Resource Center (WRC)
what: Counseling, confidential advocacy (incl. Title IX reporting site), computer pod with FREE PRINTING, lending/video library, peer support groups, SNAP application help, IMPACT mentorship program, and the Sabrina Single Parent's Scholarship.

name: LGBTQ Resource Center (Arcoíris)
what: Safe-zone environment, library, lounge, computer pod, HIV testing, confidential reporting site, social/educational events.

name: Veteran & Military Resource Center
what: Certifying official support for GI Bill/VA benefits, community space, advocacy for student veterans and military-affiliated students.

name: Accessibility Resource Center (ARC)
what: Accommodations, assistive technology, and support to create equitable learning environments.

name: Asian American Pacific Islander Resource Center
what: Cultural programming and support for AAPI students; part of UNM's resource-center network.

name: College Enrichment Program (CEP)
what: Academic support and transition programming aimed at first-generation and historically underserved incoming students.

name: Student Health and Counseling (SHAC)
what: Medical care, mental health counseling (safe-zone trained), Women's Health Clinic, Men's Health Maintenance Program.

name: Manzanita Counseling Training Clinic
what: Free, confidential counseling for individuals, couples, and families, provided by supervised counselors-in-training.

name: Engineering Student Services (ESS / ESSC)
what: Free tutoring (math, physics, engineering, English), scholarship coordination, freshman pre-major advising/orientation, peer mentoring, houses engineering student orgs, career-fair prep.

name: Society of Women Engineers (SWE) — UNM Chapter
what: Peer network, mentorship, scholarship application support, and national SWE scholarship access for women in engineering/CS.

name: Anderson School of Management — Small Business Institute
what: Free consulting work for ~25 local businesses/semester performed by supervised business students — a resume-building resource for business majors.

name: Anderson School Building — Printing Access
what: Reported by students as a location with printing access beyond the standard library quota.
contact: Anderson School of Management, main campus

name: APIConnect 'First Award' Scholarship
what: Automatic $1,000 (semester) or $500 (internship/summer) scholarship for any UNM student on an APIConnect-affiliated program — deducted directly from invoice.

name: DIWC Scholarship
what: $500 scholarship for women of color accepted to an in-person study abroad program.

name: Barry M. Goldwater Scholarship
what: Prestigious funding for STEM undergrads pursuing PhD track; UNM contact: Kiyoko Simmons.

name: Grad Studies Funding Database (Pivot)
what: Searchable database of scholarship/funding opportunities specifically for graduate students and postdocs.

name: Glenda Lewis Critical Race Scholar Award
what: Scholarship support tied to critical race scholarship/research.

name: HEERF / Federal Emergency Student Aid (historically CARES Act funds)
what: One-time emergency funds for expenses like food, housing, course materials, tech, healthcare, childcare — distributed based on FAFSA need.

name: UNM Off-Campus Housing Board
what: Structured landlord/tenant listing bulletin board for students seeking off-campus rentals.

name: Career Services Center
what: Career counseling, resume review, internship/job postings, career fairs for students/alumni.

name: Student Success Access Grant
what: Direct monetary grant for A&S students struggling financially — can be applied to Bursar balance, course fees, books, a laptop, internet access, or food. Award amount varies based on stated need.

name: Arts & Sciences Center for Academic Success (ASCAS)
what: Academic advising, retention/at-risk student support, transition courses for new/returning students (capped at 30 for individualized attention), and the Student Success Access Grant above.

name: COEHS Pathways for Academic Support and Success
what: Advising in phone, Zoom, and in-person formats (accessible for off-main-campus students); located Travelstead Hall Bldg 65.

name: College of Fine Arts Student Success & Advisement
what: Personalized advising for all Fine Arts majors on degree options, graduation requirements, and connecting to campus resources; Music dept. has its own advisement line + ARTifacts newsletter with scholarship alerts.

name: Nursing Emergency Fund
what: Emergency financial support for nursing students facing hardships (job loss, family obligations, tech access, etc.).

name: University College Advising
what: Advising home for students who haven't yet declared a major; helps explore options before committing to a specific college.

name: Global Education Office (GEO) / International Student & Scholar Services (ISSS)
what: Immigration/visa advising, work authorization (OPT/STEM OPT/Academic Training) guidance, orientation, and international admissions support.

name: CELAC (Intensive English Program)
what: Intensive English language instruction and academic English advising for international students.

name: CTL Graduate Support
what: Graduate Teaching Academy certificate, dissertation/thesis coaching, workshops, and 1:1 consultations for grad students.

name: Office of Advising Strategies / LoboTrax
what: University-wide framework connecting every college's advising center; LoboTrax degree-audit tool shows completed vs. remaining requirements.

name: School of Law Emergency Financial Aid Fund
what: Emergency financial aid up to $1,000 per eligible student — covers things like temporary housing/essential needs after displacement (e.g. fire) or other crises.

name: Keller & Keller Scholarship
what: $3,000-$5,000 awarded to 3 first-year law students with financial need who are interested in representing injured persons (personal injury law).

name: Bar Exam Prep Scholarships (various NM State Bar sections)
what: Multiple scholarships to help defray bar-exam study costs; example: M&A Gross Indian Self Determination Fund gives $1,500 to two 3Ls for first-time NM Bar takers.

name: Resource Center for Raza Planning (RCRP) & AICAE student chapter
what: RCRP connects planning coursework to traditional NM community development work. AICAE (American Indian Council of Architects+Engineers) provides a peer support network across Architecture, Engineering, and design fields.

name: SAAP Graduate Assistantships
what: Grad students in good standing can apply for assistantships (tuition/stipend support in exchange for work).

name: Honors College Student Support Directory
what: Curated one-stop list linking Honors students directly to ARC, Afro, AISS, Food Pantry, Career Services, CAPS, CEP, Community Engagement Center, El Centro, LGBTQ RC, Mentoring Institute, Rec Services, SHAC, OWL Writing Center, VRC, and WRC.

name: Center for Academic Program Support (CAPS)
what: Umbrella tutoring/academic-support center, including the Online Writing Center (OWL) for free writing tutoring.

name: Mentoring Institute
what: Coordinates mentoring programs and research across campus; connects students to structured mentorship.

name: Community Engagement Center
what: Connects students to service-learning, volunteering, and community-based projects — a bridge between UNM and Albuquerque community orgs (relevant to the 'half university half public' bucket).

name: UNM Taos Emergency Funds + Student Resource Navigator
what: Dedicated staff member (Student Resource Navigator) helps connect students to emergency funds, SNAP, WIC, food pantries, and local shelters — a single point of contact model.

name: PASOS Resource Center Campus Food Pantry
what: On-campus food pantry with quick meals, take-home groceries, hygiene products, and kitchen appliances (microwave, fridge, coffee maker, toaster) for immediate use.

name: UNM-Valencia Community Resources Guide
what: Localized PDF directory covering Los Lunas/Belen-area food pantries (St. Vincent De Paul), Income Support Division offices, WIC, and health clinics — separate from main-campus Albuquerque resources.

name: UNM-Gallup Office of Financial Aid
what: Local financial aid office handling FAFSA, grants, loans, and work-study specifically for the Gallup branch.

name: Community Food Pantry (Gallup)
what: Food pantry serving the Gallup area, relevant to UNM-Gallup students.

name: Self Help, Inc.
what: Economic-insecurity support including food/shelter assistance for Los Alamos area, relevant to UNM-Los Alamos students.

name: Lobo Food Pantry — Pack a Luminaria / Holiday Meals in a Bag
what: Seasonal donation drives (Thanksgiving/winter break) supplementing the main Lobo Food Pantry with pre-made holiday meal bags.

name: Dean of Students Emergency Scholarship
what: Up to $1,000, deposited directly to the student (not applied to Bursar balance) for genuine personal emergencies — can cover housing, transportation, groceries for a household, and similar essentials. Not for general ongoing financial hardship.

name: ASUNM Emergency Scholarship & Advocacy Scholarship
what: Student-government-administered emergency and advocacy scholarships — separate funding pool from Dean of Students or college-specific funds.

name: El Centro External Scholarship Hub
what: Curated list of external scholarships channeled through El Centro, incl. Hispanic Scholarship Fund, LNESC, ScholarSHPE, The Dream US Scholarship (undocumented/DACA students), Immigrants Rising Scholarship, Albuquerque Community Foundation scholarships, Daniels Boundless Opport...

name: Center for Financial Capability Scholarship Index
what: Master index page linking to scholarship/funding pages by college: Honors, Nursing, Pharmacy, Population Health, Law, Medicine, Engineering, Emergency Funding, College of Education, Anderson, LGBTQ RC, Dean of Students Short-Term Loans, El Centro, ASUNM, and the UNM Fund.

name: Diane J. Klepper, MD Student Affairs Endowment
what: Funds peer tutoring assistance, board review course support, and aid for a student's family or personal emergency issues — flexible, discretionary use by Student Affairs Office.

name: La Tierra Sagrada Society Scholarships
what: Need-based scholarships for medical students; 100% of contributions go directly to scholarships/endowment.

name: College of Pharmacy Scholarships
what: Approximately $200,000 awarded annually across PharmD students, mostly semester-to-semester; plus the donor-funded 'Circle of Joy' fund specifically supporting students during their final-year advanced practice pharmacy experiences.

name: Division of Dental Hygiene (Dept. of Dental Medicine)
what: Competency-based dental hygiene education with clinical training; program has decades of history and connects students to professional development opportunities.

name: College of Population Health Scholarships
what: Scholarships for both undergraduate and graduate Population Health programs.

name: School of Public Administration (SPA) Semester Awards
what: Awards of up to $3,600/semester based on academic accomplishment and/or financial need — a notably large per-semester amount compared to most college-level funds in this dataset.

name: Sandra B. Weeke Scholarship
what: Scholarship specifically for MPA students who are single parents, commemorating SPA alumna Sandra B. Weeke.

name: AMIGO Scholarship
what: Study abroad funding resource administered through GEO, mentioned as a funding option for SPA/other students studying internationally.

name: HELP New Mexico, Inc. (HELPNM)
what: Much bigger than its name suggests: 25 offices, 200+ employees, serving 10 NM counties (incl. Bernalillo). Six service pillars — Employment, Education, Income/Asset Building, Housing, Health/Behavioral, and Civic Engagement — plus free food via the Child & Adult Care Food Prog...

name: Storehouse New Mexico
what: One of NM's largest food pantries — 'client choice model' (shop like a grocery store) provides a full cart of groceries incl. meat/dairy/produce; also runs a Pet Food Pantry on the 3rd Friday monthly and can assist with water bills. Fed nearly 78,000 people in 2025.

name: Rio Grande Food Project
what: Provides a week's worth of groceries once a month (30 days apart); no documentation strictly required, though photo ID + proof of guardianship for kids under 18 requested. Also assists with water bills.

name: Storehouse West
what: Monthly food package (canned goods, grains, legumes, canned meat/fruit/veg) plus a Kids Clothing Closet (newborn-18) with jeans, shoes, jackets, etc.

name: Enlace Comunitario
what: Free, bilingual (Spanish/English) domestic violence intervention: legal assistance for protective orders and family-law representation, individual/group therapy for victims and children, limited transitional housing/rent/utility/deposit assistance, parenting classes, and refer...

name: Albuquerque Family Advocacy Center (AFAC)
what: Single physical location combining on-site partners for domestic violence, child abuse, and sexual assault victims — includes Enlace Comunitario and the NM Asian Family Center among on-site/off-site partners.

name: New Mexico Asian Family Center (NMAFC)
what: The only agency in NM providing culturally tailored advocacy and support programming specifically for the Pan-Asian community — fills a gap the rest of this dataset doesn't otherwise cover.

name: Jewish Community Center (JCC) of Greater Albuquerque
what: Fitness/aquatics facilities, early childhood education, day camps, and — notably — the Jewish Care Program offering emergency assistance, resource/referral, support groups, and senior outreach. Also documented as supporting Saranam and several food banks directly.

name: Hillel at UNM
what: Shabbat services and home-cooked kosher meals, holiday observances, social functions, retreats, Hebrew/Bible courses, and community service opportunities for Jewish students.

name: Islamic Center of New Mexico (ICNM)
what: The largest/oldest mosque in Albuquerque, serving 2,000+ Muslims; daily prayers, Friday Jum'ah, a children's Sunday school (Madrassat Umar al-Islamia), and community events open to Muslims and non-Muslims alike. Located near UNM and the airport.

name: MINARA Muslim Community Center
what: Beyond worship, runs concrete direct-service programs: homeless feeding, health & wellness classes, language arts/calligraphy, and youth martial arts/archery programs.

name: First Nations Community HealthSource
what: 50+ years serving the urban Native community with culturally-centered healthcare: multiple clinic locations (Zuni, Truman, Central, Vision), a dedicated Traditional Wellness Program, dental, counseling, and diabetes/nutrition education. Open to non-Native patients too, as an F...

name: Albuquerque Indian Center (AIC)
what: Historically provided wrap-around services (counseling, DWI/substance abuse counseling, DV counseling, weekly AA meetings, food/hygiene boxes, resume help, legal services via UNM Law Clinic) to the urban Native community.

name: National Indian Youth Council / Native Professional Advancement Center
what: Workforce development and employment services for Native Americans, funded partly via Dept. of Labor grants; despite the 'Youth' name, serves adults broadly through the Native Professional Advancement Center.

name: City of Albuquerque Office of Native American Affairs
what: Coordinates between the City and NM Tribal governments; maintains the Commission on American Indian & Alaska Native Affairs (CAIANA) and a directory of NM Pueblos/Tribes/Nations contacts.

name: Adelante Development Center
what: One of NM's largest nonprofits (top-10 non-govt employer in the state) — senior day programs, assisted living homes, employment services, transportation/meal services at senior centers, and DiverseIT (free/low-cost computers for people with disabilities and nonprofits, includi...

name: ARCA (Albuquerque Resource Center for the Advancement of the Disabled)
what: 24/7 supported living/residential services, intermediate care, family living placements, and vocational training (e.g., La Paloma Greenhouse horticulture program, ARCA Janitorial Services for employment) — serves 600+ individuals of all ages including seniors.

name: NM Division of Vocational Rehabilitation (NMDVR)
what: State/federally funded program helping people with documented disabilities get and keep employment — individualized planning, a dedicated Vocational Rehabilitation Counselor, assistive technology access, job placement partnerships with employers, and Pre-Employment Transition ...

name: NM Dept. of Veterans' Services (NMDVS) — Benefits Overview
what: 16 field offices statewide staffed by Veteran Service Officers (veterans themselves). Key benefits: full property tax exemption for 100% disabled veterans (partial for others, $4,000 reduction), full state income tax exemption on military retirement pay, reduced-fee hunting/fi...

name: NM Veterans' Dependents Tuition Waiver
what: Full tuition waiver (matriculation fees, room, board, books, supplies) for dependent children of veterans killed in action or who died of battle wounds.

name: NM Vietnam Veterans' Scholarship
what: Covers tuition, fees, and books for one academic year (renewable with satisfactory progress) at state-funded schools for undergraduate, master's, or doctoral programs.

name: In-State Tuition & State Financial Aid for Undocumented Students
what: NM is classified a 'Comprehensive Access' state — undocumented residents (including DACA recipients) are eligible for in-state tuition, state financial aid, professional/occupational licensure in most professions, and driver's licenses.

name: NM Standard Driver's License for Non-Citizens
what: NM has offered driving privileges to undocumented residents since 2003 (current rules per 2019's SB 278) — one of only two states (with WA) issuing a single, non-distinguished license usable for boarding domestic flights, not just driving.

name: State-Funded Healthcare Access for Non-Citizens
what: As of July 2025, NM grants state-funded healthcare access to all non-citizens including undocumented immigrants; federal Medicaid eligibility still varies by immigration status separately.

name: Undocumented UNM (undocumented.unm.edu)
what: Centralized hub for undocumented students and their families covering admissions/enrollment/financial aid, campus & community resources, legal support, donations/fundraising, and legislative action tracking. UNM police are barred from contacting/detaining/questioning/arresting...

name: New Mexico Immigrant Law Center (NMILC)
what: Makes immigration legal help affordable/accessible for NM's immigrants and aspiring citizens; promotes knowledge of legal rights and the immigration process regardless of ability to pay.

name: UNM Law School Community Lawyering Clinic
what: Supervised law students represent clients applying for DACA, U-visas, work authorization, and adjustment of status — free legal services via a teaching clinic model.

name: Somos Un Pueblo Unido
what: Immigrant-led organization promoting worker and racial justice; provides information (not direct legal representation) on immigrants' rights, civil rights, fair housing, tenant law, and workers' rights, plus wage-theft support in Northern NM.

name: Lutheran Family Services Rocky Mountains (LFS) — Refugee & Asylee Program
what: Full wraparound resettlement case management: housing, ESL classes, job placement/career advancement, a savings-match program, small-business loans, farm-plot access (Tres Hermanas Farm), and summer-school programming. Has resettled 3,000+ refugees in NM over the past decade a...

name: Partnership for Community Action (PCA)
what: Builds strong communities in Albuquerque's South Valley and statewide, focused on education, economic sustainability, wellness, and immigrant rights advocacy/leadership development.

name: Prosperity Works
what: Builds economic prosperity for limited-income NM families through financial education, asset planning, and family supports — policy advocacy plus direct capacity-building for partner orgs.

name: Rio Grande Credit Union — Juntos Avanzamos Program
what: First credit union in Albuquerque (2nd in NM) certified 'Juntos Avanzamos' ('Together We Advance') — lets anyone open a real bank account without a Social Security Number, using an ITIN plus a government photo ID (Matrícula Consular, foreign passport, foreign driver's license,...

name: ITIN Banking — General Access Explainer
what: An Individual Taxpayer Identification Number (ITIN), issued by the IRS regardless of immigration status, can substitute for an SSN at many banks/credit unions nationally (not just Juntos Avanzamos-designated ones) — enabling checking/savings accounts, some credit cards, and ev...

name: Nusenda Credit Union — UNM Student Union Branch
what: On-campus credit union branch inside the SUB; not immigrant-specific, but relevant as an accessible campus banking option alongside Rio Grande Credit Union's immigrant-focused services elsewhere in town.

name: City of Albuquerque Office of Immigrant & Refugee Affairs
what: Dedicated city office maintaining a running list of resources for refugees and immigrants in the Albuquerque metro area, plus a directory of partner agencies and translation services.

name: El CENTRO de Igualdad y Derechos
what: Distinct from UNM's 'El Centro de la Raza' — a community-based organizing group predominantly staffed by immigrant leaders, focused on grassroots organizing, policy advocacy, leadership development, and voter engagement for low-wage immigrant workers.

name: Immigrant and Refugee Resource Village of Albuquerque (IRRVA)
what: Free vocational skills training (sewing, weaving, beading, needle-arts) for economic empowerment, one-on-one adult basic literacy and ESL tutoring, and community education about immigrant/refugee contributions and needs. Serves low/no-income families often with no formal educa...

name: United Voices for Newcomer Rights (UVNR)
what: Partners directly with UNM to improve newcomer health/social determinants of health, provides individual advocacy and mentorship, works on cultural appropriateness of early childhood/K-12 education, runs a Youth Community Advisory Council for newcomer youth leadership developm...

name: NM Working Families Tax Credit — ITIN Filers Included
what: NM's state-level Earned Income Tax Credit equivalent, currently 25% of the federal EITC amount, EXPLICITLY includes ITIN filers as eligible (HB 291, 2021) — unlike the federal EITC, which excludes ITIN filers entirely. Also extended eligibility to workers age 18-24.

name: Federal Tax Credits Still Available to ITIN Filers
what: While ITIN filers CANNOT claim the federal EITC, they CAN still claim: the Child and Dependent Care Credit (up to $1,050-$2,100), the $500 Credit for Other Dependents (for a qualifying ITIN-holding relative, including children over 17 or ITIN-holding kids not eligible for the ...

name: UNM ITIN Application Guidance
what: Explains what an ITIN is/isn't (IRS purposes only — doesn't grant work authorization, immigration status, or Social Security benefits) and how to apply via IRS Form W-7 (also available in Spanish as Form W-7SP).

name: Homewise ITIN Mortgage Loans
what: Cross-reference: Homewise (already in this dataset for down-payment assistance and no-PMI mortgages) explicitly offers ITIN loans — mortgage lending using an ITIN instead of an SSN, opening a path to homeownership for ITIN holders specifically.

name: Fair Housing Act Protections for Applicants Without an SSN
what: Landlords CAN legally ask for an SSN and CAN require extra documentation from applicants without one, but CANNOT deny housing based on national origin or immigration status — that's illegal discrimination under the Fair Housing Act. An ITIN, income proof, photo ID, and referen...

name: NM Business Registration Without an SSN
what: New Mexico does NOT require an SSN to register a business or pay state business taxes — sole proprietors can use an ITIN, and registered entities (LLC, corp, partnership) register separately. An ITIN alone does not authorize traditional W-2 employment, but it does allow self-e...

name: Emergency Medicaid Coverage for Undocumented Residents
what: Undocumented New Mexicans are eligible for EMERGENCY coverage only through NM's Medicaid program — this is narrower than full Medicaid and narrower than the 'state-funded healthcare for all non-citizens' policy logged in an earlier pass, which should be reconciled/clarified wi...

name: DACA Coverage Bridge (status uncertain as of Aug 2026)
what: A federal rule (Marketplace Integrity and Affordability Rule) removed DACA recipients' eligibility for BeWell marketplace coverage and Premium Tax Credits effective Oct 1, 2025. NM HCA created a temporary 'DACA Coverage Bridge' offering a Clear Cost Gold Plan, but enrollment f...

name: BeWell NM Marketplace — No SSN Required (but not ITIN either)
what: Important nuance: applicants without an SSN can still apply to BeWell by leaving the SSN field blank — but an ITIN is explicitly NOT accepted in that field either. Instead, eligibility runs through proof of an eligible immigration status/document. This means ITIN alone does no...

name: CNM Food Pantry (4 campus locations)
what: Free bag of fresh fruits/vegetables and non-perishables at 4 locations across the city (Main Campus SRC, SV II Room 198, MJG Cafe Westside, G Building). Uses PantrySoft for check-in/online ordering, registered once per semester. Also occasional Suncat Salon vouchers.

name: Rust Opportunity Assistance Fund
what: Emergency financial assistance for CNM students facing unforeseen financial obstacles (car repairs, medical bills, unexpected housing costs, etc.).

name: Wellness CNM — Case Management & Free Counseling
what: Case managers/social work interns for 1:1 needs navigation (healthcare, utility assistance, housing referrals, food); 6 FREE counseling sessions per student via Hope Forward Therapy; on-campus BeWell NM Marketplace enrollment help every Tuesday.

name: THRIVE Program
what: Specialized wraparound support (advising, tutoring, wellness/financial resource connections, gas/groceries/emergency funds via grant funding) specifically for students who were in the foster care system.

name: F.I.R.S.T. Program
what: Specialized wraparound support (advising, tutoring, financial/wellness resource connections) specifically for formerly incarcerated students re-entering education.

name: CNM Foundation Fund Directory (Basic Needs Fund, Annual Fund, etc.)
what: Umbrella of donor funds beyond the Rust Fund: the Basic Needs Fund (general basic-needs support), Annual Fund (flexible support where needed most), plus memorial/program-specific funds.

name: Public Library of Albuquerque & Bernalillo County — Free Computer/Printing/Notary/Job Search
what: Free WiFi and computer/internet access at every branch (Microsoft Office included); printing at $0.15/page; free fax and copier service; free notary services at select branches; dedicated Job & Career Guide (resume books, quiet study rooms, career databases); tax prep help dur...

name: Library Job & Career Guide — 'Working It Out!'
what: Curated guide to city/county/state job postings, resume-writing resources, career databases, and desktop/office services (PCs, printers, fax, quiet study rooms) specifically framed around job searching.

name: The Food Depot
what: Santa Fe's equivalent to Roadrunner Food Bank — distributed 28.3M+ lbs of food since 2000 (37.7M+ meals). Runs the Food Mobile (walk-on trailer serving Santa Fe/Rio Arriba counties + Northern Pueblos), large drive-through pantries, a Food 4 Kids school-based backpack program (...

name: St. Elizabeth Shelter & Supportive Housing
what: 24/7/365 emergency shelter for adult men (up to 4 months, waitlist process); Casa Cerrillos permanent supportive housing for disabled single men/women with case management and life-skills training; Santa Fe Suites permanent supportive housing for singles/couples. Outreach serv...

name: City of Santa Fe Food Benefits & Support + CONNECT Network
what: City-run hub listing food pantries (Food Depot, Bienvenidos Outreach, several church pantries) plus the CONNECT Network — navigators linking residents to food, housing, and other support services with a bilingual (English/Spanish) resource directory.

name: Santa Fe County Food Resources Hub
what: County-run coordination page connecting residents to Food Depot distributions, community resources, and support services countywide (not just city limits).

name: Sandoval County Community Services Department
what: County-run umbrella covering Community Health Services (incl. a Health Care Assistance Program), Senior Services (congregate/home-delivered meals, transportation, case management, Senior Volunteer Program), Behavioral Health referrals, Juvenile Justice Services, and Permanent ...

name: Meadowlark & Broadmoor Senior Centers
what: Two no-cost senior centers offering fitness classes, educational seminars, social events, weekday meals, day trips, financial guidance, and volunteer opportunities for adults 55+.

name: Valencia Shelter Services (VSS)
what: 24-hour crisis line, emergency shelter, rental assistance, case management, life skills and job readiness training, individual/group counseling — program available for up to two years for DV survivors.

name: NM Health Care Authority Field Offices — Rio Rancho & Los Lunas
